newsitem.title: CANADA: Reuters bond pricing application rejected.
newsitem.headline: Reuters bond pricing application rejected.

text.p: The Investment Dealers Association of Canada on Wednesday rejected an application by Reuters Holdings Plc to provide Canadian bond pricing services in competition with CanPX Corp.

The application was rejected at a meeting of the IDA's board of directors. In denying the application, the IDA said "Reuters failed to demonstrate satisfactorily that it can perform transparency-related services as effectively as CanPX."
A Reuters spokesman said the company was disappointed by the decision and an appeal to the Ontario Securities Commission (OSC) could be expected.
"Although we regret having to do so, it's our present intention to proceed with an appeal to the OSC," said John Reid-Dodick, corporate counsel with Reuters America Inc.
The creation of CanPX was approved by the Ontario Securities Commission last May. The bond pricing service was created with the goal of increasing transparency in Canadian bond and money markets.

The creation of CanPX was opposed by bond broker Cantor Fitzgerald, which sells its bond pricing information to Reuters for distribution worldwide. In its decision to create CanPX, the OSC gave the IDA the power to approve competitors with CanPX.

In rejecting the Reuters application, the IDA said a single composite feed, incorporating information from all available inter-dealer bond brokers, would not likely be available if the Reuters application were approved.
Approval of the Reuters application would also likely fragement available market information and force users to subscribe to multiple services to create a comprehensive composite, the IDA said.

Reuters believes its application to compete with CanPX would provide the required transparency, said Reid-Dodick. He noted that the Reuters application had the support of organizations such as the Ontario Financing Authority.

Reuters' application "would have provided advanced transparency for the Canadian debt markets as a product both of Reuters' own extensive worldwide distribution system and the creative arrangement that we anticipated with the Toronto Stock Exchange," said Reid-Dodick.
